summary: Washington County, AL former lookout site registered in 2019; the register says only the stands remain, plus a vandalized former communications building.

facts.status_note: Register says the stands are all that remain, and a heavily vandalized building that once held communication equipment is also on the site

events.note: Registered September 15, 2019 on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register; nominated by Andrew Zerbe

evidence.supports: administered by the Alabama Forestry Commission
the stands are all that remain
heavily vandalized building that once held communication equipment is on the site
evidence.quote: Also on site is heavily vandalized building that used to hold communication equipment.
over 200 of these artifacts dotted Alabama

evidence.supports: aircraft as the most common explanation for the decline
evidence.quote: The most common explanation is that aircraft was more efficient in spotting fires in a much broader area than a 100-foot tower could provide.

evidence.supports: Alabama retains about a third of the lookouts it once had
evidence.quote: Today, Alabama retains only about a third of the lookouts it once had.

sources.title: Thomas Kaufmann: Keeping Alabama's historic lookout towers

notes_for_editor: The only tower-specific source is the Former Fire Lookout Sites page, whose description is one short sentence plus a building note. It does not say what the stands are, so the story does not guess whether any part of the tower remains. The Kaufmann column (source 2) is general context, not about this site. Two web searches gave no build date, design, staffing or fire history, and none is written. Access is not established. The NHLR URL guessed at nhlr.org/lookouts/us/al/milstead-fire-tower-site/ returned 404 in the crawl cache; that does not prove the site is absent from NHLR.
